context: The text gives the hash function as key % capacity, where % denotes the remainder and bucket indices start at 0. The figure labels the left side “Hash table capacity = 100” and the right side “Hash table capacity = 200.” The arrow between them shows that the capacity doubles. The table below gives the old and new positions of four pairs.
description: The figure compares only the bucket distributions before and after expansion. It specifies neither a particular order for moving entries nor a structure for storing colliding entries. Before expansion, 236 is drawn outside the bucket to indicate that it collides with 136 in bucket 36. It does not occupy a separate bucket. Ellipses stand for the remaining buckets.
prose.result: Expansion can lower the load factor and, in this example, eliminates the original collision. It cannot guarantee that every input will be free of collisions.

steps.announcement: Before expansion, the capacity is 100, and keys 136 and 236 collide in bucket 36.
steps.explanation: Before expansion, the capacity is 100. With key % 100, 136:A and 236:D collide in bucket 36. Bucket 50 holds 550:B, and bucket 83 holds 783:C.
steps.key_state: Capacity 100. In bucket 36, 136:A and 236:D collide. Bucket 50 holds 550:B, and bucket 83 holds 783:C.
steps.title: Before expansion: capacity 100, collision in bucket 36

steps.announcement: After expansion to 200, recompute the remainder for every key. Key 236 stays in bucket 36. Keys 136, 550, and 783 move to buckets 136, 150, and 183, respectively. This resolves the collision in the example.
steps.explanation: The capacity doubles to 200. Recomputing all four indices with key % 200 leaves 236:D in bucket 36 and moves 136:A to bucket 136, 550:B to bucket 150, and 783:C to bucket 183. Each pair now occupies a different bucket. The collision is resolved, and each key retains its value.
steps.key_state: Capacity 200. Buckets 36, 136, 150, and 183 hold 236:D, 136:A, 550:B, and 783:C, respectively.
steps.title: After expansion: capacity 200, entries rehashed

prose.summary: After the capacity changes, recompute the bucket indices to preserve key-value pairs and reduce collisions.
prose.title: Expanding and rehashing a hash table
